page.layout: One column of running text, with a running head at the top and a catchword and gathering signature at the foot. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Psal. xix, 2, -7. Cœli enarrant gloriam Dei, &c. Sol est tanquam Sponsus prodiens è thalamo suo : lætatur decursurus viam, &c. Job. ix, 7. Observanda interim Miracula, Jos. x, 13, 14. & Ief. xxxviii, 7. Pro vario hujus motû variæ sunt influentiæ ; speciatim ratione tempestatum anni: sic tamen, ut effecta subjaceant Arbitrio & Providentiæ Dei: Hos. 2, 21, 22. Dictum Iehovæ ; exaudiam Cœlos; & ipsi exaudient Terram; & Terra exaudiet frumentum, &c. Levit. xxvi, 19. Reddam Cœlum ut ferrum ; & terram , ut æs. Adde Gen. viii, 22. Psal. lxv, 10. Jud. v, 20.

Vanæ autem sunt Astrologicæ prædictiones Gentilium: Deut. xviii, 10. Nam 1. Deo proprium est, Corda scrutari, & dirigere. 2. Immateriales operationes ad materiales causas referri non debent. 3. Non omnes effectus naturales indè certò prædici possunt, quantò minùs liberi.

Piè & prudenter tamen de Signis extraordinariis, Cometis, & similibus, judicandum est. Joël. 2, 29, 30. Act. 2, 19, 20. Edam ostenta in Cœlis, &c. collatâ experientiâ omnium sæculorum, & observatione prudentum.
main_text.head: XXXI. Ex Doctrinâ Spiritûs Sancti.
main_text.p: 1. Agnoscendum est tale Systema Mundi, ut Terra non sit, nec unquàm fuerit, Sidus ; sed cum Aquis inferioribus quàm maximè distincta sit à Cœlis & Expanso: Sol verò, & Luna, reliquæque Stellæ, dispositæ in Expanso, ad afferendum lucem super Terram, &c. Gen. I, 1, 2; 6, -9; 14, -18.

2. Globum Terræ non moveri ; sed quiescere, & stabilem esse; atque istâ ratione distingui ab Aquis, Aëre, Sole, &c. Psal. xciii, 1. Etiam firmavit orbem, ne se moveat. 3. Elevaverunt Flumina fluctus suos. Eccl. 1, 4, -7, Generatio (una) labitur, & (altera) generatio advenit: Terra autem in sæculum stat. Oritur Sol, & occidit Sol. Subinde circumeundo pergit ventus, & ad circuitus suos revertitur ventus. Omnia Flumina pergunt ad Mare.

page.notes: Printed "s" in the Latin is rendered as plain s throughout. Two small marks in the left margin near the line "motû" and at the foot ("O 4", "ad") are uncertain; the foot mark is read as the signature and the catchword. The printed passage in the last paragraph contains a line with a stroke under "Mare" that may be a catchword or a correction; the line is transcribed as printed. Small circle and figure at the foot may be a printer's mark. No marginal notes are printed on this page.
